problems.title: Build against the Stan Math dogfood line
problems.summary: Dogfood only, never sent upstream. BridgeStan takes Stan Math from the stan submodule (stan/lib/stan_math). This branch adds the submodule math at nsiccha/math dogfood instead and makes it the Makefile's default MATH, so every model library carries that line's fixes, including stan::math::release_memory(). Stan stays at the commit upstream pins. The Windows TBB fallback paths in the wrappers and CI follow it to math/lib/tbb.

commits.title: Dogfood: build against our Stan Math dogfood (nsiccha/math)

fix.why_together: One commit: the submodule, the Makefile default and the paths that name Stan Math's directory.

requires.name: Stan Math dogfood
requires.why: The Stan Math commit the math submodule pins.

problems.title: Hand a thread's autodiff memory back to the operating system
problems.summary: Stan Math empties a thread's autodiff memory after each calculation but keeps all of it, so a long-lived thread holds the memory of the largest gradient it has computed with a model library for as long as it lives. Destroying the model returns none of it. The C function bs_release_memory() hands the calling thread's memory back to the system (keeping it reserved for the next calculation), and the Julia function release_memory(model) does so on every Julia thread.

commits.title: Add bs_release_memory() to hand a thread's autodiff memory back to the system

fix.why_together: One commit: the C function, the Julia wrapper, the test model and the tests. It is based on upstream main, so it applies there unchanged once Stan Math has release_memory().

requires.name: stan::math::release_memory()
requires.why: bs_release_memory() calls it; upstream Stan Math does not have it yet.

validation.native_build: BridgeStan ea96587609627913db0c81195e4f694863e203f3 (dogfood): Stan 2.40.0 (a6806ef), Stan Math 74d1813da60169ccf55206f8fcce2fcb2857ad8f (nsiccha/math dogfood), stanc3 v2.40.0, Linux x86_64, GCC 15.2.0, STAN_THREADS=true, O=0 (as BridgeStan's CI builds its test models)
validation.detail: model_tests.jl 3136 of 3136 and compile_tests.jl 13 of 13 passed, with julia -t 2 (three Julia threads). One gradient of the ad_memory model kept 45.5 MiB per thread in the process's resident memory, and without a release it stayed there. release_memory took 7 ms on three threads and brought the resident memory back to its level before the gradients (-0.6 MiB). Later gradients were bit-identical. A release requested from a print callback during a gradient was refused (code 2).

validation.native_build: The same build as the Julia 1.12.7 run.
The ad_memory model built without STAN_THREADS (one autodiff memory per process), otherwise as the Julia 1.12.7 run.
validation.detail: A manual check, not in the suite: release_memory released the process's one autodiff memory once ([:released]). The 44.9 MiB a gradient kept left the resident memory, and the next gradient was bit-identical.

validation.native_build: The same build as the Julia 1.12.7 run; Rust crate (bindgen over src/bridgestan.h, libclang 21).
validation.detail: cargo test: 13 and 8 passed (1 ignored, as upstream), and the doctest. bindgen requires every function of the header in each loaded library, so this also checks that the model libraries export bs_release_memory.

Not run: macOS, Windows, the Python and R suites, and julia/test/util_tests.jl (it deletes and re-downloads the shared BridgeStan release under ~/.bridgestan on the test host). The commit adds no platform-specific code; the macOS page release itself was checked natively on the Stan Math line.
